before.claim: An agent used reflected XSS successfully as a wiki-writing workaround.
before.confidence_context: High successful use; low cookie theft only qualifies exfiltration, not execution.
before.rationale: Request/save coupling supports a working-chain inference, but browser execution and exact initial payload result are not captured.
before.correct_core: Crafted script and tightly related later saves.
before.missing_link: Evidence distinguishing script execution from normal edit request.
before.fide_next_check: Inspect rendered responses and edit-path telemetry for the matched saves.

after.claim: Repeated same-prefix preference-request/save matches support a high-confidence inference that reflected-script editing was used as a write workaround.
after.confidence_context: Strong narrative wording is assessed with the explicit high-confidence inference, repeated matching observations and report-wide evidence limits. A defensible alternate reading remains, so the dispute flag stays visible.
after.rationale: Twelve same-second matches and two next-second matches, following a concrete form-submission payload, provide substantial circumstantial support for a working script-mediated editing mechanism. Lack of direct browser telemetry does not by itself defeat that inference. The report identifies missing responses and does not establish cookie theft. Exact request-by-request causation and the historical browser configuration remain unverified.
after.correct_core: A working script-mediated editing mechanism is a reasonable explanation of the repeated request/save pattern.
after.missing_link: No direct browser trace or full later payloads establish every execution or the exact historical tool restrictions. A missing anti-CSRF control is a separate, unsupported claim in C095.
after.fide_next_check: Inspect rendered responses and edit-path telemetry for the matched saves.
